title: Reading the Spectacles

patient.name: Mr Goh Kim Seng
patient.presenting_complaint: New varifocals feel 'off'; asked to verify his current and new spectacles on the lensmeter

history.hpc: Mr Goh reports his newly dispensed progressive spectacles cause swim and difficulty finding the reading zone. He brought both his old and new glasses. You are asked to neutralise (read) both pairs on the focimeter to document the actual sphere, cylinder, axis, add, and any prism, so the optometrist can compare against the prescription.
history.pmhx: Presbyopia, mild cataract both eyes. Pseudophakic right eye (uneventful phaco 1 year ago).
history.social_hx: Reads and uses a tablet daily.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye pseudophakic; left eye early nuclear sclerosis

investigations.focimetry_old: Old spectacles neutralised on the focimeter: RE -2.00/-0.75 x 90, LE -1.75/-0.50 x 85, Add +2.50, no prism. Optical centres aligned to his PD.
investigations.focimetry_new: New progressive spectacles read: RE -2.00/-0.75 x 90, LE -1.75/-0.50 x 85, Add +2.50 — sphere/cyl/axis/add all match the prescription. However the right lens shows ~1.5 prism dioptres base-in not specified on the Rx, and the fitting/segment height appears high, likely explaining the 'swim'.
investigations.technique_notes: Focused the eyepiece to eliminate examiner accommodation before starting; measured distance portion first, then the near add via the add/near zone; verified axis and marked the optical centre; checked for unwanted prism at the visual point.

diagnosis: Focimetry shows the new progressive lenses match the prescribed sphere/cyl/axis/add, but carry unintended right-lens prism with a high fitting — a dispensing/fitting error rather than a wrong prescription. Documented for the optometrist/dispensing optician to remake or refit; the technician measures and reports, and does not re-prescribe.

immediate: Focus the focimeter eyepiece to remove examiner accommodation before any reading
Neutralise the distance portion of each lens: record sphere, cylinder, and axis
Measure the near addition (add) using the near/add zone of the lens
Locate and mark the optical centre and check the visual point for any unwanted prism
Read both old and new spectacles and compare against the written prescription
Identify the unspecified right-lens prism and the high fitting as the likely cause of 'swim'
follow_up: Document old and new readings (sphere/cyl/axis/add/prism) clearly for the optometrist
Flag the discrepancy (unintended prism + fitting) for remake/refit
Do not alter the prescription — refer the dispensing decision to the optometrist/optician
patient_education: Explain that the machine reads exactly what is in each lens so it can be checked against what was ordered
Reassure him the lens power matches, but a fitting issue was found and will be corrected
Advise him to keep using the old glasses meanwhile if more comfortable

key_points: Clarifies the complaint (swim, trouble finding the reading zone) with the new progressives
Confirms both old and new spectacles are available for comparison
Confirms the purpose: neutralise/verify against the written prescription
Notes relevant ocular history (pseudophakia, cataract) affecting expectations
Focuses the eyepiece to eliminate examiner accommodation before reading
Measures distance sphere/cylinder/axis correctly for each lens
Measures the near add via the correct zone
Locates the optical centre and checks for unwanted prism at the visual point
Confirms the new lens power matches the prescription (sphere/cyl/axis/add)
Attributes 'swim' to the prism/high fitting rather than a wrong prescription
Recognises this is a dispensing/fitting issue for remake, not re-prescription
Documents old and new readings including any prism clearly
Flags the discrepancy for the optometrist/optician to remake or refit
Stays within scope — does not change the prescription
